name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A light motorcycle whose motor produces 5 horsepower (3,750 W) or less: an electric two- or three-wheeler lands here when it exceeds a moped's 2 horsepower or 30 mph. Defined by Hawaii Revised Statutes §286-2 and §291C-1 as "motor scooter", which HB 2021 (Act 259, signed July 15, 2026) renamed "motor-driven cycle" throughout the traffic, licensing and insurance statutes.

restrictions.rule: Handlebars and a seat the rider straddles, on no more than three wheels, or a federally certified three-wheeled autocycle
Its motor produces 5 horsepower (3,750 W) or less; a moped is excluded
An electric two-wheeler over 2 horsepower (1,500 W), or one that can go faster than 30 mph, is a motor-driven cycle rather than a moped
Riders need a motorcycle license (category 2); an instruction permit requires a state-approved basic motorcycle rider course, and its holder can't ride after dark or carry passengers
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a safety helmet fastened with a chin strap
Riders and passengers must wear safety glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windscreen
Registered with the county director of finance and must pass a safety inspection every year once it is two years past its first sale
Must carry liability insurance of at least $20,000 per person, $40,000 per accident and $10,000 property damage
Not allowed in bike lanes or on bike paths; one whose electric motor can exceed 28 mph is also an electric motorcycle
Freeway entrances are posted against vehicles of less than 5 horsepower
